raw:
{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "Feasible with single-column ELM snow physics; SNOTEL comparison requires external observational data ingestion.",
    "answerable": [
      "Simulated peak snow water equivalent (SWE) at each SNOTEL-collocated column",
      "How peak SWE and timing scale along the Wenatchee basin elevation gradient",
      "Snow accumulation and melt-out dates per elevation band",
      "Partitioning of precipitation into snow vs rain across elevation"
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "Direct in-model comparison to SNOTEL: ELM outputs must be compared to SNOTEL records in post-processing (model does not assimilate obs)",
      "Basin-integrated snow distribution / lateral snow redistribution (single-column has no lateral transport)",
      "Sub-grid orographic precipitation enhancement beyond what the atmospheric forcing resolves"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 5,
  "n_justification": "Five columns collocated with established Wenatchee-basin SNOTEL stations spanning ~980 m to ~1860 m capture the elevation gradient (rain-snow transition, mid-elevation deep snowpack, and high-elevation persistent snow), enabling a station-by-station model-vs-SNOTEL evaluation of peak SWE.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "fish_lake_980m", "lat": 47.8217, "lon": -120.7783, "soil_texture": "sandy loam"},
    {"id": "stevens_pass_1238m", "lat": 47.7472, "lon": -121.0894, "soil_texture": "loam"},
    {"id": "trinity_1447m", "lat": 48.0197, "lon": -120.8697, "soil_texture": "gravelly loam"},
    {"id": "grouse_camp_1670m", "lat": 48.0000, "lon": -120.8500, "soil_texture": "sandy loam"},
    {"id": "lyman_lake_1859m", "lat": 48.1717, "lon": -120.8983, "soil_texture": "gravelly sandy loam"}
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "2000",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2014",
    "STOP_N": "15",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "2000-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "H2OSNO", "SNOWDP", "SNOW", "RAIN", "SNOWLIQ", "SNOWICE",
      "QFLX_SNOMELT", "QSNOMELT", "FSNO", "SNOWNODE",
      "TSA", "TG", "TSOI", "FSDS", "FLDS", "QRUNOFF"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": [
    "ELM single-column (PTS_MODE) snow physics (multi-layer SNICAR-enabled snowpack)",
    "Elevation-appropriate atmospheric forcing (GSWP3 or downscaled/lapse-rate-corrected reanalysis) at each site",
    "External SNOTEL SWE observation records (NRCS) for post-processing model-obs comparison"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "Atmospheric forcing air temperature and precipitation are lapse-rate corrected to each column's true elevation to represent the gradient realistically",
    "Peak SWE is diagnosed as the annual maximum of H2OSNO for each water year (Oct 1 - Sep 30)",
    "Model spin-up prior to 2000 is sufficient; first year treated as spin-up and excluded from peak-SWE statistics",
    "Vegetation/PFT at each site set to evergreen needleleaf forest transitioning to open subalpine at highest elevation, consistent with Cascade land cover",
    "SNOTEL station coordinates are approximate to within the NRCS-published locations"
  ]
}

feasibility.verdict: Feasible with single-column ELM snow physics; SNOTEL comparison requires external observational data ingestion.
answerable: Simulated peak snow water equivalent (SWE) at each SNOTEL-collocated column
How peak SWE and timing scale along the Wenatchee basin elevation gradient
Snow accumulation and melt-out dates per elevation band
Partitioning of precipitation into snow vs rain across elevation
not_answerable: Direct in-model comparison to SNOTEL: ELM outputs must be compared to SNOTEL records in post-processing (model does not assimilate obs)
Basin-integrated snow distribution / lateral snow redistribution (single-column has no lateral transport)
Sub-grid orographic precipitation enhancement beyond what the atmospheric forcing resolves

parsed.n_justification: Five columns collocated with established Wenatchee-basin SNOTEL stations spanning ~980 m to ~1860 m capture the elevation gradient (rain-snow transition, mid-elevation deep snowpack, and high-elevation persistent snow), enabling a station-by-station model-vs-SNOTEL evaluation of peak SWE.
requires_capabilities: ELM single-column (PTS_MODE) snow physics (multi-layer SNICAR-enabled snowpack)
Elevation-appropriate atmospheric forcing (GSWP3 or downscaled/lapse-rate-corrected reanalysis) at each site
External SNOTEL SWE observation records (NRCS) for post-processing model-obs comparison
assumptions: Atmospheric forcing air temperature and precipitation are lapse-rate corrected to each column's true elevation to represent the gradient realistically
Peak SWE is diagnosed as the annual maximum of H2OSNO for each water year (Oct 1 - Sep 30)
Model spin-up prior to 2000 is sufficient; first year treated as spin-up and excluded from peak-SWE statistics
Vegetation/PFT at each site set to evergreen needleleaf forest transitioning to open subalpine at highest elevation, consistent with Cascade land cover
SNOTEL station coordinates are approximate to within the NRCS-published locations
